scenes.title: At the Iron Gate
scenes.summary: F1 brings tea to the courtyard table as M3 uses her three simple sentences to break the ice with M4.
scenes.intro: Out under the shade tree at the {SHOW} in {CITY}, older brother {M4} stands stiffly in his grey coat across from {M3} as {F1} sets down a hot teapot and steps back. Listen to the whole scene first.
story: So 'someone with something from Grandfather' was you all along, {M3}.
Hello, {M4}. Thank you for coming today.
I recognized your neat block handwriting on that postcard in two seconds.
Wait—you knew it was from me and came anyway?
Of course I came. Why did you hide behind a mystery note?
Because I was afraid you were still angry. I missed you these three years.
Three stubborn years... honestly, little brother, I missed you too.
Excuse me, gentlemen—here is hot tea, and warm lemon cake is on the way.
Lemon cake? Wait—how did she know about Friday lemon cake?
Sit down, {M4}, take off your heavy coat, and look at this blue suitcase.
Is that the old dark-blue bag from Grandfather's workshop?
Take all the time you need—the courtyard is yours.
scenes.outro: {M4} recognized {M3}'s handwriting in two seconds and came anyway! Next time, they open the white paper parcel under the courtyard tree.

scenes.title: The Wooden Train
scenes.summary: M3 hands M4 their grandfather's carved wooden train just as childhood piano teacher F3 steps over to greet them.
scenes.intro: Seated at the round courtyard table, {M3} opens the dark-blue suitcase and lifts out the parcel wrapped in white paper for {M4}, while {F3} walks gently across the stones toward them. Listen first.
story: Before the movers cleared {STREET}, I saved this box from the attic shelf.
Open the white paper... no! Grandfather's carved wooden locomotive!
Look underneath the wheels—your name and mine are still pencilled there.
I thought this was lost when we sold the house! Why keep it for me?
Because a house is brick and timber, {M4}, while family is what we keep.
And you two boys kept the best part of Number twelve right here.
Excuse me, madam... wait. That voice! Madam {F3}, my piano teacher?!
Still waiting for you to play your F-major scale slowly, {M4}!
Am I dreaming?! Did you plan this whole reunion, {M3}?
Pure luck—and one swapped blue suitcase on Monday morning's train!
Life arranges better duets than we do, my dear boys.
Please sit with us, Madam {F3}! Tell me I am not twenty-five years late for my lesson!
scenes.outro: Grandfather's wooden train is home, and {M4}'s astonishment at seeing Madam {F3} filled the whole courtyard with laughter. Inside at the desk, however, {M2} is still staring at that letter. See you next time.

scenes.title: Thirty Days on Paper
scenes.summary: Behind the front desk M2 laments the sale notice while M1 and F1 urge him not to give up without reading the fine print.
scenes.intro: Back behind the front desk, {M2} sits slumped beside the brass key board while {M1} and {F1} lean over the counter speaking in low voices. Listen first.
story: Fifteen years of polishing brass keys and straightening ties... gone in thirty days!
Stop burying us before we read the whole document, {M2}.
Yes! Earlier I noticed a second page clipped behind the cover letter.
Legal paragraphs give me a headache even with two pairs of glasses!
This house survived eighty winters and one broken boiler valve yesterday.
Wait—who is sitting ten metres away in our courtyard right now?
An architect who works with historic courtyard buildings all over {CITY}!
Smart thinking, {F1}. {M3} reads city building rules every single week.
Oh, I could never bother a paying guest with our landlord troubles!
After we guarded his blue suitcase all week? He will want to help!
Wait—here comes {F2} back from their table right now.
scenes.outro: {F1} remembered they have an expert on historic courtyard buildings sitting right under their tree! Next time, {F2} serves the lemon cake and {M4} senses something is wrong inside.

scenes.title: Lemon Cake and Sharp Eyes
scenes.summary: Enjoying F2's warm lemon cake, M4 notices the worried faces inside the lobby window and offers help.
scenes.intro: Out in the courtyard, {F2} sets down a plate of warm glazed lemon cake for {M4} and {M3}. Between bites, observant older brother {M4} glances toward the lobby window. Listen first.
story: Fresh from the oven: Friday lemon cake with extra corner pieces!
One bite... {M3}, close your eyes! That tastes exactly like Linden Lane!
{F2} baked it this morning when Madam {F3} told her our Friday story.
What kind of magical guesthouse did you stumble into, little brother?
The kind that fixes attic lamps in the rain and guards a stranger's bag.
Then tell me why the poor gentleman behind the front desk looks ready to cry.
Oh! Did you see {M2} through the window? I tried to smile doubly wide!
{F2}, is something wrong inside? Did the boiler pipe leak again?
Worse than a pipe... a registered letter came from the building owner at noon.
A property letter? Let {M3} and me see it—I work in municipal contracts, and he knows heritage law!
Wait, {M4}—you still work at City Hall's contract desk?!
Both of you?! Leave your teacups—come inside this very second!
scenes.outro: Not only is {M3} a historic courtyard architect, {M4} works at City Hall's municipal contract desk! Let's hurry inside to the front desk next time.

scenes.title: Page Two, Clause Fourteen
scenes.summary: Examining page two of the letter, M3 points out Heritage Clause 14 protecting historic buildings with public ground-floor cafés.
scenes.intro: At the front desk, {M2} hands the two-page notice to {M3} while {F1} holds her breath beside the reservation ledger. {M3} flips immediately to the second sheet. Listen first.
story: Look at page one, {M3}: 'commercial office conversion next month.' We are finished!
Wait a moment, sir—did you read page two clipped underneath?
Only small grey numbers! My heart stopped at page one!
Look where {M3} is pointing with his pencil, {M2}!
Clause fourteen of the {CITY} Old Quarter Act—and my brother outside just nodded!
In plain words, please! What does Clause fourteen say?
No courtyard building over eighty years old may become private offices if the ground floor serves neighbours daily.
'Serves neighbours daily'—like a public morning café?!
Exactly! Right now your four tables only serve overnight hotel guests.
Wait—if we open our courtyard gate every morning for neighbourhood coffee and bread...
Then your guesthouse lease is protected for another ten years by city law!
{M2}! Your glasses just fell off your nose for a happy reason!
scenes.outro: Page two changed everything: opening the four-table breakfast corner to the neighbourhood saves the {SHOW} for ten years! Next time, {M2} has two big announcements in the café.

scenes.title: Permanent Keys
scenes.summary: Beaming with relief, M2 greenlights F2's morning courtyard café and offers F1 the permanent front-desk job.
scenes.intro: In the sunlit café corner, {M2} stands tall in front of {F2} and {F1} with page two of the letter still in his hand and a huge grin on his face. Listen first.
story: {F2}, how many cinnamon rolls and lemon cakes can your oven bake each morning?
Double what I make now! Are we really opening the courtyard café to our street?
Starting tomorrow at eight! Four tables inside, three tables under the tree!
My dream café—right here in our own courtyard! Wait until I tell the baker's market!
And now, {F1}, today is Friday—the last day of your five-day trial week.
Oh! With the suitcases, the boiler, and the letter, I completely forgot!
On Monday you opened our sticking door; since then you saved rooms, pipes, breakfast, and our lease.
If you do not hire her full-time, {M2}, I am hiring her in my kitchen!
Hands off, {F2}! {F1}, would you stay as our permanent front-desk manager?
Stay here with all of you? Yes—a hundred times yes!
Wonderful! Your name goes in {M1}'s big paper book in permanent ink!
Best first week of my life!
scenes.outro: A neighbourhood courtyard café for {F2} and a permanent front-desk job for {F1}! Next time, dusk falls and the courtyard lanterns light up for everyone.

scenes.title: Under the Golden Lanterns
scenes.summary: As evening lanterns glow across the courtyard, F1, F3, and M4 toast the week's unexpected friendships.
scenes.intro: Warm dusk settles over {CITY}, and strings of golden paper lanterns glow above the courtyard tree. {F1}, {F3}, and {M4} share tea and music memories in the evening air. Listen first.
story: Look up at those golden lanterns against the evening sky—how peaceful!
To think on Monday morning {M3} picked up the wrong blue bag on Platform Two.
If he had picked up the right bag, none of us would be standing here tonight!
My teacup survived, two brothers made peace, and {F1} found a new home.
Madam {F3}, {M3} and I booked a quiet dinner nearby—will you join us tomorrow?
Gladly, {M4}, as long as nobody talks about selling old pianos!
And tomorrow morning at eight, your first courtyard coffees are on the house!
We will bring half of City Hall to {F2}'s tables next week, I promise.
Listen—even the buzzer from room four has been quiet all evening!
Do not tempt it, Madam {F3}! I am almost fond of those two rings now.
Here is to the {SHOW}—the loudest quiet place in {CITY}!
To good neighbours, warm bread, and open gates!
scenes.outro: Golden lanterns overhead, old friends reunited, and tomorrow's courtyard café ready to open at eight! One final scene remains in Season 1—and {M1} just found something strange in the cellar. See you next time.

scenes.title: Room Nine
scenes.summary: Fetching spare café chairs from the cellar, M1 uncovers a locked wooden crate stamped 'Room 9' and a ninth brass key.
scenes.intro: Late Friday night after the courtyard empties, {F1} and {M2} are closing the front desk when {M1} climbs up from the back cellar carrying extra café chairs—and a dusty wooden box. Listen first.
story: Did you find the three folding chairs behind the boiler room, {M1}?
Found the chairs—and behind an old brick partition, I found this.
A small cedar chest? I have never seen that box in fifteen years!
Brush the dust off the brass plate on top... wait, read that number!
Let me pull my glasses down from my forehead... 'Room Nine'?!
{M1}, look at the wooden key board behind us: one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight!
This guesthouse has only ever had eight rooms! Where on earth is Room Nine?!
Listen when I tilt the box—something metal just slid inside.
There is a tiny keyhole on the front latch, and look taped underneath: an old brass key!
A ninth brass key?! Do we open it tonight or wait until morning?!
Look at the folded blueprint sticking out of the hinge—there is a hidden door drawn on this floor!
Grab the flashlight, both of you—my second week starts right now!
scenes.outro: A ninth brass key, a dusty cedar box stamped 'Room 9', and a blueprint showing a hidden door on the ground floor! Season 1 of {SHOW} is complete—see you in Season 2!
